seoTitle: How to Use Zapier with Notion (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Connect Notion to Zapier to automatically create or update database items whenever new data arrives from your other apps.
intro: Keeping a Notion workspace current by hand becomes a chore once you're juggling multiple databases. This guide shows how to connect Notion to Zapier, authenticate your workspace, and map incoming data into specific Notion property types so pages and database items update themselves.

steps.heading: Create a new Zap
steps.body: Open the Zapier dashboard and start a new workflow.

steps.heading: Select Notion
steps.body: Choose Notion as your trigger or action app and review the available events.

steps.heading: Authenticate your Notion account
steps.body: Sign in and grant workspace access permissions, selecting the specific pages you want to connect.

steps.heading: Select your database and properties
steps.body: Choose your target database, specific page, and custom property layouts.

steps.heading: Fetch sample data
steps.body: Pull fresh database sample data payloads for real-time field testing.

steps.heading: Map fields and finish setup
steps.body: Add an action step to create or update a database item, mapping data into property types like Select, Multi-Select, Text, Dates, and Relations.

faq.question: Can Zapier create new items in a Notion database automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, you can use the Create Database Item action to add new entries whenever your trigger app sends new data.

faq.question: What Notion property types can I map data into?
faq.answer: You can map data into property types like Select, Multi-Select, Text, Dates, and Relations.

faq.question: Can I trigger a Zap when a Notion item is updated?
faq.answer: Yes, Updated Database Item is one of the available trigger events for Notion.

faq.question: Do I need to give Zapier access to every page in my workspace?
faq.answer: No, you select the specific database, page, and property layouts you want to connect during setup.
